name: Two-Path Shelling Compatibility Conflict
definition: Let $K_1=\langle ab,bc\rangle$ and $K_2=\langle de,ef\rangle$ be paths on disjoint vertices, distinguished at $ab$ and $de$. Their assembly has facets $F_1=bcde$, $F_0=abde$, and $F_2=abef$.
properties: The local shellings $(bc,ab)$ and $(de,ef)$ combine as $(F_1,F_0,F_2)$. The equally valid local choices $(bc,ab)$ and $(ef,de)$ cannot be preserved by any global shelling: they force $F_1,F_2$ before $F_0$, although $F_1\cap F_2$ is only an edge rather than a ridge. This is the smallest illustration of conflicting active records.
